data.title: Back to Top Button
data.tagline: Return quickly to the top of a long page
data.description: A back-to-top control is useful after substantial scrolling, especially when important navigation sits at the top. Keep it out of the way and reveal it only after the user has moved far enough. It does not solve a poorly structured page.

use: A page whose main controls are at the top
avoid: Show it before the user scrolls
Use it on a short page
Cover mobile content or another floating action
Treat it as a replacement for clear navigation and sections

lessonPractice.title: A long mobile product list often requires returning to filters at the top, and a support entry already occupies the bottom-right. How should Back to top work?

options.label: Reveal a clearly named button after meaningful scrolling and keep it clear of support and bottom actions
options.feedback: It appears only when long-distance return is useful, and collision avoidance keeps both controls usable.

options.label: Show the button on every page at all times, including before any scrolling is possible
options.feedback: Short pages have no return need, so a persistent button adds noise and consumes limited mobile action space.

options.label: Place it over the bottom-right support control and raise its layer so it receives clicks first
options.feedback: Layer order only chooses which control covers the other; it does not keep both entries visible and usable.

data.agentPrompt: Show a Back to top button after the product list scrolls beyond one screen and return users to the filter area. Avoid support and bottom purchase actions, hide it on short pages, and test mobile safe areas, keyboard focus, and reduced motion.
